newsitem.title: USA: Lenders file default on DreamWorks proiect-reports.
newsitem.headline: Lenders file default on DreamWorks proiect-reports.

text.p: A consortium of lenders led by Chase Manhattan Bank has filed a notice of default on DreamWorks' proposed Playa Vista project, the Daily Variety publication said on Wednesday.
The filing means the Chase-led consortium, which includes Bank of America and Sanwa Bank, could foreclose on the project or initiate a bank sale after 110 days, the report said.

The project consists of more than 1,000 acres set aside in West Los Angeles to develop a high-tech film studio for DreamWorks SKG, the entertainment venture formed by Steven Spielberg, Jeffrey Katzenberg and David Geffen.

The Playa Vista project is owned by Los Angeles developer Maguire Thomas Partners and Howard Hughes Corp, which is a unit of Rouse Co of Columbia, Maryland, the Wall Street Journal said in its electronic edition Wednesday.
The Journal said Maguire has been negotiating recently for a new deal with Goldman Sachs & Co, Morgan Stanley & Co and others.
Variety said the loans involved total about $150 million plus interest.
